purpose: A minimal two-column statement block: an eyebrow label opposite a two-line h2. The smallest real section on the site.

headingLines.note:
Exactly 2 lines separated by a
. Measured: "On-brand visuals." (2) and "Made by AI." (3).

anchorId.note: The section carries id="what-is-fourmula", which is the target of the hero's scroll cue.

evidence.structure: Structure, layout and motion measured against the live original. A pixel audit verified 1382/1382 elements at a 1440px viewport and 962/962 at 390px with zero deltas. Copy is the original's own.

constraints.verification: src/pages/Home.jsx:13 renders <What /> second. Checked against all 5 real templates: it appears only in `home`, immediately after hero.home.

motion.detail: The h2 carries data-flash, so public/motion/m22.js splits it into .flash-word spans and m23.js reveals them on a ScrollTrigger: opacity 0 -> 1 at #F94A00 over 0.2s power2.out, then to #FD7B03 over 0.05s, then to var(--fonts-100) over 0.1s.
motion.reducedMotionFallback: Render the heading as one unsplit block at text.primary and full opacity, with no colour sequence.
motion.reducedMotionFallbackKind: design-rule (the source ships NO prefers-reduced-motion handling for this section, so the fallback is prescribed by this repository, not mirrored)

responsive.base: two columns: eyebrow left, heading right
responsive.max-767px: heading.display drops to 2.25rem and label.tag to 1rem

contentMaxWordsTotalNote: Set BETWEEN the measured real total and the maximum the per-field budgets allow, so the cap can actually reject an over-long instance instead of being unreachable. extraction/verify_all.py check [p] fails if any declared contentMaxWordsTotal becomes vacuous (>= the per-field maximum). Previously 13, which was unreachable.
